messages:
maria: quick heads up — saw a spike in quota-mapping errors after the client library bump (ts + py) this morning. console shows a bunch of requests with policy=unknown.

anand: ugh, repro? logs?

maria: minimal repro attached in the logs channel but essentials: requests with the policy toggle header sometimes arrive as boolean `true` and sometimes as string `\"true\"`. console parser expects the string and treats bare booleans as missing -> unknown quota mapping.

jeremy: is this a client serialization difference between ts and py?

maria: yeah — ts SDK ended up emitting the raw boolean (from the JS options) while python `requests` serialization turned it into a string. Both were valid HTTP headers but console's parser only handled string values.

anand: can you paste the header examples?

maria: sure:

```http
x-rw-policy-toggle: true   # from TS client
x-rw-policy-toggle: "true"  # from Python client
x-rw-policy-version: v2
```

shay: deploy-bot just showed the api-tests failing: `quota-mapping.test: expected mapped quota, got unknown` in CI.

deploy-bot: pipeline: api-tests-umbrella failed (quota-mapping.test) — link: https://ci.internal/runs/9987 :x:

jeremy: easy short-term fix is to make the console accept both `true` and `\"true\"` (normalize to string). That buys us time. Long-term we should standardize the header contract.

anand: Agreed. Two possible remediation paths: (A) server-side normalization (fast), (B) patch all SDKs to always stringify toggle flags (breaking-ish but minimal). I lean both: normalize server-side + patch SDKs in a non-breaking minor release to stringify.

maria: the tricky bit is rollouts: we have customers pinned to older SDK versions. If we change server behavior to coerce booleans to strings, that's safe. If we change SDKs to stringify, we need telemetry + rollout window to verify nothing else relied on boolean header shape.

shay: UX question for console: can we show a deprecation banner when we parse a boolean header and map it? i.e., telemetry + warning in the dashboard for requests that used boolean form. That would help customers find callers.

jeremy: +1. Add telemetry event `policy.header_shape` with values `string|boolean|other` and expose a small alert tile in Console->Routes so PMs can contact integrators.

anand: implementation plan I propose:
1) server: normalize incoming header to string immediately (hotfix) — roll tomorrow canary -> global.
2) console: accept both shapes and emit `policy.header_shape` telemetry. add a small dashboard tile for 2 weeks.
3) SDKs (ts/py/go): patch to stringify toggle flags, semver-minor release with clear changelog + migration note.
4) 30-day deprecation window after telemetry shows ~95% string usage, then consider making server stricter if needed.

maria: sounds good. estimate for server hotfix?

anand: I can do a patch this afternoon, canary by EOD, global tomorrow morning.

shay: I'll scope the console tile — small PR to telemetry + UI, should be a half-day if we reuse the metering tile.

jeremy: I'll open the TS PR and mark it as non-breaking (stringify at header serialize point). Will run integration tests against server-canary.

maria: created issue + tracking PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/712 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ts/pull/1456 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-py/pull/789 — linking in case people want to follow.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: api-normalize-headers -> canary cluster at 2026-03-21T18:30Z.

maria: thanks everyone. follow-ups: please add a short note in changelog and an example snippet showing header shape. :thumbsup:

jeremy: will do — want to keep the client change behind a feature flag for 1 week to observe.

anand: good call. I'll wire a `policy_header_strict` feature flag on the server for toggling acceptance mode during the window.

shay: filing a quick customer comms blurb in #marketing-distro to warn integrators.

maria: closing loop here — will update thread when canary metrics look good (quota mapping failures drop to 0).
